title: Pointing words
blurb: This, that, these and those: learn the table, then use the words in sentences.

hero.title: This, that, these, those
hero.text: A pointing word shows which thing or person you mean. It is fixed: its last letter never changes.

hero_html:
STAGE 3 · UNIT 3

This, that, these, those

A pointing word shows which thing or person you mean. It is fixed: its last letter never changes.

هَذَا

src.text: Arabic has a word for near things and a word for far things. Each one also changes for male, female and plural.

src.title: Learn the last vowel too
src.text: {هَذَا} ends in alif, {هَذِهِ} and {هَؤُلَاءِ} in kasra, {ذَلِكَ}، {تِلْكَ}، {أُولَئِكَ} and {هُنَاكَ} in fatha. These endings never change.

blocks.html: Learn the last vowel too. هَذَا ends in alif, هَذِهِ and هَؤُلَاءِ in kasra, ذَلِكَ، تِلْكَ، أُولَئِكَ and هُنَاكَ in fatha. These endings never change.
blocks.text: Learn the last vowel too. هَذَا ends in alif, هَذِهِ and هَؤُلَاءِ in kasra, ذَلِكَ ، تِلْكَ ، أُولَئِكَ and هُنَاكَ in fatha. These endings never change.

src.text: {هَؤُلَاءِ} and {أُولَئِكَ} are for groups of people, male or female: {هَؤُلَاءِ طُلَّابٌ}، {هَؤُلَاءِ نِسَاءٌ}. For plural things Arabic normally uses {هَذِهِ}: {هَذِهِ كُتُبٌ} "these are books".

blocks.html: Tip: هَؤُلَاءِ and أُولَئِكَ are for groups of people, male or female: هَؤُلَاءِ طُلَّابٌ، هَؤُلَاءِ نِسَاءٌ. For plural things Arabic normally uses هَذِهِ: هَذِهِ كُتُبٌ "these are books".
blocks.text: Tip: هَؤُلَاءِ and أُولَئِكَ are for groups of people, male or female: هَؤُلَاءِ طُلَّابٌ ، هَؤُلَاءِ نِسَاءٌ . For plural things Arabic normally uses هَذِهِ : هَذِهِ كُتُبٌ "these are books".

src.text: Look at the noun after the pointing word. Does it have {ال}?

items.title: No ال: a sentence
items.text: "This is a book." {هَذَا} is the Topic and {كِتَابٌ} is the Information.

items.title: With ال: a phrase
items.text: "this book". It is not finished yet. Add Information: {هَذَا الْكِتَابُ جَدِيدٌ}.

blocks.text: No ال: a sentence هَذَا كِتَابٌ "This is a book." هَذَا is the Topic and كِتَابٌ is the Information. With ال: a phrase هَذَا الْكِتَابُ "this book". It is not finished yet. Add Information: هَذَا الْكِتَابُ جَدِيدٌ .

items.note: {هَذَا الْبَيْتُ} is the Topic part. {قَرِيبٌ} is the Information.

blocks.html:
هَذَا بَيْتٌ.
This is a house.
A full sentence.
هَذَا الْبَيْتُ قَرِيبٌ.
This house is near.
هَذَا الْبَيْتُ is the Topic part. قَرِيبٌ is the Information.
تِلْكَ سَيَّارَةٌ.
That is a car.
A full sentence.
تِلْكَ السَّيَّارَةُ جَدِيدَةٌ.
That car is new.
تِلْكَ السَّيَّارَةُ means "that car".
blocks.text: هَذَا بَيْتٌ. This is a house. A full sentence. هَذَا الْبَيْتُ قَرِيبٌ. This house is near. هَذَا الْبَيْتُ is the Topic part. قَرِيبٌ is the Information. تِلْكَ سَيَّارَةٌ. That is a car. A full sentence. تِلْكَ السَّيَّارَةُ جَدِيدَةٌ. That car is new. تِلْكَ السَّيَّارَةُ means "that car".

src.text: To say "this is THE book", put {هُوَ} or {هِيَ} in the middle: {هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ}، {هَذِهِ هِيَ السَّاعَةُ}.

src.text: Choose the pointing word by the noun you point to. Is it near or far? Male or female? One or a group of people?

blocks.text: Choose the pointing word by the noun you point to. Is it near or far? Male or female? One or a group of people?

items.en: This is a pen and this is a watch.
That is a mosque and that is a school.
These are students and those are men.

items.note: {بِنْتٌ} has no {ة}, but it is feminine. Use {هَذِهِ}.

blocks.html:
هَذَا قَلَمٌ وَهَذِهِ سَاعَةٌ.
This is a pen and this is a watch.
قَلَمٌ is masculine, سَاعَةٌ is feminine.
ذَلِكَ مَسْجِدٌ وَتِلْكَ مَدْرَسَةٌ.
That is a mosque and that is a school.
Far: ذَلِكَ for masculine, تِلْكَ for feminine.
هَؤُلَاءِ طُلَّابٌ وَأُولَئِكَ رِجَالٌ.
These are students and those are men.
Groups of people: هَؤُلَاءِ، أُولَئِكَ.
هَذِهِ بِنْتٌ.
This is a girl.
بِنْتٌ has no ة, but it is feminine. Use هَذِهِ.
blocks.text: هَذَا قَلَمٌ وَهَذِهِ سَاعَةٌ. This is a pen and this is a watch. قَلَمٌ is masculine, سَاعَةٌ is feminine. ذَلِكَ مَسْجِدٌ وَتِلْكَ مَدْرَسَةٌ. That is a mosque and that is a school. Far: ذَلِكَ for masculine, تِلْكَ for feminine. هَؤُلَاءِ طُلَّابٌ وَأُولَئِكَ رِجَالٌ. These are students and those are men. Groups of people: هَؤُلَاءِ ، أُولَئِكَ . هَذِهِ بِنْتٌ. This is a girl. بِنْتٌ has no ة , but it is feminine. Use هَذِهِ .

src.text: A pointing word is fixed, but it still has a job. The job gives it a place. The noun after it shows the ending that the pointing word cannot show.

items.note: {هَذَا} is the Topic. Fixed, in the place of rafʿ.
{هَذَا} is the doer. Place of rafʿ. See the damma on {الرَّجُلُ}.
{هَذَا} is the object. Place of naṣb. See the fatha on {الْبَابَ}.
{هَذَا} comes after a preposition. Place of jarr. See the kasra on {الْبَيْتِ}.
{هَذَا} is the owner. Place of jarr.

blocks.html:
هَذَا كِتَابٌ.
This is a book.
هَذَا is the Topic. Fixed, in the place of rafʿ.
دَخَلَ هَذَا الرَّجُلُ الْمَسْجِدَ.
This man entered the mosque.
هَذَا is the doer. Place of rafʿ. See the damma on الرَّجُلُ.
فَتَحَ الطَّالِبُ هَذَا الْبَابَ.
The student opened this door.
هَذَا is the object. Place of naṣb. See the fatha on الْبَابَ.
فِي هَذَا الْبَيْتِ
in this house
هَذَا comes after a preposition. Place of jarr. See the kasra on الْبَيْتِ.
كِتَابُ هَذَا الطَّالِبِ
this student's book
هَذَا is the owner. Place of jarr.

See the kasra on الْبَيْتِ . كِتَابُ هَذَا الطَّالِبِ this student's book هَذَا is the owner. Place of jarr.

src.title: The words for "these two" change
src.text: {هَذَانِ} (two males) and {هَاتَانِ} (two females) are flexible. In naṣb and jarr they become {هَذَيْنِ} and {هَاتَيْنِ}. You learn them with the dual in Stage 4.

src.title: In short
items: Choose by the noun: near or far, male or female, one or a group of people.
{هَذَا كِتَابٌ} is a sentence. {هَذَا الْكِتَابُ} is a phrase: "this book".
Pointing words are fixed, but they have a place: rafʿ, naṣb or jarr.
{هَذَانِ} and {هَاتَانِ} are not fixed. They wait for Stage 4.

blocks.html:
In short

  1. Near: هَذَا، هَذِهِ، هَؤُلَاءِ. Far: ذَلِكَ، تِلْكَ، أُولَئِكَ. Place: هُنَا، هُنَاكَ.
  2. Choose by the noun: near or far, male or female, one or a group of people.
  3. هَذَا كِتَابٌ is a sentence. هَذَا الْكِتَابُ is a phrase: "this book".
  4. Pointing words are fixed, but they have a place: rafʿ, naṣb or jarr.
  5. هَذَانِ and هَاتَانِ are not fixed. They wait for Stage 4.
